meta.face: Two clearly different Syrians with warm olive-brown skin. ABRAHAM (left): about sixty-five, with a LONG, NARROW face and a PROMINENT, KNOBBY CHIN that juts forward below a lean jaw — a high, lined forehead, large, dark, heavy-lidded eyes under thin, curved grey brows, a long, thin, straight nose, a wide, thin-lipped mouth; bald crown with grey-black hair falling straight to the shoulders; a THIN grey-black beard trimmed SHORT along the jaw so that the knobbed chin shows; the gaze grave and gentle, on Mary. MARY (right): about twenty-seven, with a ROUND, SOFT face — a broad, smooth brow, wide-set, large, dark eyes wet with tears, straight dark brows, a short nose with a rounded tip, full cheeks, a small, full mouth, a small, round chin; dark hair hidden under the veil; the gaze lowered in contrition.
meta.basis: No likenesses survive; the Menologion of Basil II (Wikipedia's lead image) shows Abraham as an elderly grey-bearded monk before a building. The book tells the walled-up cell with its small window, Mary's cell beside his, and her return; its engraving shows him at his cell door and her kneeling at hers. The knobbed chin and the round young face are our choices.
